PART VI: THE STATES [Article 152-237]

Article Mapping from Union to State level:

  • Articles 73-111 (Parliament) → Add 89 → gives corresponding articles of State Legislature.
  • Articles 112-213 → Add 90 → Corresponding articles for State Legislature.

Key Replacements:

  • President → Governor
  • Parliament → State Legislature
  • Prime Minister → Chief Minister
  • Council of Ministers (Union) → Council of Ministers (State)
  • Attorney General of India → Advocate General of State
  • Consolidated Fund of India → Consolidated Fund of State

Chapter II: State Executive (Articles 153-167)

  • Consists of (Governor + CM + CoM + Advocate General)

Article 153: Governor of States

  • There shall be a Governor for each State.
7th Constitutional Amendment allowed for the appointment of same person as the Governor of two or more states.

Article 154: Executive Power of State

  • Executive power of State vests in the Governor.
  • Can be exercised directly or through subordinate officers.

Article 155: Appointment of Governor

  • Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

Article 156: Term of Office of Governor

  • (1) Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
  • (2) Governor may, address his resignation to the President
  • (3) Term: 5 years from the date of assuming office, subject to earlier removal or resignation.

Article 157: Qualifications for Appointment as Governor

  • Must be a Citizen of India and should have completed 35 years of age.

Article 158: Conditions of Governor's Office

  • (1) Governor cannot be a member of Parliament or State Legislature; must vacate seat before entering office.
  • (2) Governor cannot hold any office of profit.
  • (3) Governor is entitled to use official residence without rent; emoluments and privileges as determined by the Parliament.
  • (3A) If serving multiple states, emoluments are shared as per Presidential order.
  • (4) Emoluments and allowances cannot be reduced during his tenure.

Article 159: Oath or Affirmation by Governor

  • Oath administered by Chief Justice of High Court, or in absence, senior-most judge.

Article 160: Discharge of Governor's functions in contingencies

  • President can appoint a person to discharge functions of Governor during contingencies.

Article 161: Power of Governor to Grant Pardons

  • Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions, or commute sentences.
  • But he cannot:
  • Pardon death sentence (only President can).
  • Use pardoning power against Martial Court sentences.

Article 162: Extent of Executive Power of State

  • State's executive power extends to matters on which the State Legislature can make laws.

Article 163: Council of Ministers to Aid and Advise Governor

  • Council of Ministers, headed by Chief Minister, aids and advises the Governor.
  • Advice of Council of Ministers is not binding on the Governor.

Article 164: Other Provisions as to Ministers

  • (1) Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor; other Ministers appointed on CM's advice.
  • (2) Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state.
  • (3) Ministers must take oaths of office and secrecy as administered by the Governor.
  • (4) A Minister who is not elected as MLA/MLC within 6 consecutive months ceases to be a Minister.
  • (5) Salaries and allowances determined by State Legislature.

Article 165: Advocate General for the State

  • (1) Appointed by Governor; must be qualified to be a High Court judge.
  • (2) Advises State Government on legal matters.
  • (3) Holds office till the Governor's pleasure.

Article 166: Conduct of Business of State Government

  • All executive actions must be expressed in the name of Governor.

Article 167: Duties of Chief Minister

  • Communicate decisions of Council of Ministers to Governor.

Chapter III: State Legislature (Articles 168-212)

Article 168: Constitution of Legislatures in States

  • (1) Every State shall have a Legislature, consisting of the Governor.
Structure diagram: Governor at top, with LC (Legislative Council, Upper House/Permanent House) and LA (Legislative Assembly, Lower House) below.
  • All states have a Legislative Assembly. (Unicameral legislature)
  • 6 States have a Legislative Council as well. (Bicameral legislature)
Andhra PradeshMaharashtra
BiharKarnataka
TelanganaUttar Pradesh

States with (Legislative Assembly + Legislative Council):

TRICK - KABUTM
K - Karnataka
A - Andhra Pradesh
B - Bihar
U - Uttar Pradesh
T - Telangana
M - Maharashtra
3 UTs out of 8 have LA, i.e. Delhi, Puducherry, J&K.

Article 169: Abolition or Creation of Legislative Councils

  • Parliament can create or abolish Legislative Councils just by Simple Majority, based on a resolution passed by the State Legislative Assembly by Simple Majority.
  • Such a law is not considered an amendment under Article 368.

Article 170: Composition of Legislative Assemblies

  • (1) Legislative Assembly: not less than 60 and not more than 500 members should be elected by direct election.
  • (2) Constituencies should have roughly equal population-seat ratio.
  • Special case:
  • Goa, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim → Minimum 30 members
  • Mizoram → 40 members; Nagaland → 46 members

Article 171: Composition of Legislative Councils

  • (1) Total members shall not exceed 1/3rd of Legislative Assembly, minimum 40 members. (Indirectly Elected)
  • (3) Of the total no. members of the LC of a state:
  • (a) 1/3rd elected by members of local authorities (municipalities, district boards, etc.).
  • (b) 1/12th elected by Graduates of 3 years or more.
  • (c) 1/12th elected by Teachers with at least 3 years experience.
  • (d) 1/3rd elected by Legislative Assembly members.
  • (e) 1/6th nominated by Governor (experts in literature, science, art, cooperative movement, social service) — LiSAS+ Cooperative movement

Article 172: Duration of State Legislatures

  • (1) Legislative Assembly term = 5 years from first meeting, unless dissolved earlier.
  • (2) Legislative Council: Permanent body; 1/3rd members retire every 2 years. (Hence, term of a member = 6 years)

Article 173: Qualifications for Membership

  • (a) Must be a citizen of India.
  • (b) Minimum 25 years for Legislative Assembly, 30 years for Legislative Council.
  • (c) Must possess other qualifications prescribed by Parliament.

Article 174: Sessions, Prorogation, Dissolution

  • (1) Governor summons house of the Legislature; maximum gap between two sessions is 6 months.
  • (2) Governor can:
  • (a) prorogue Houses or
  • (b) dissolve Legislative Assembly.

Article 175: Governor's Address and Messages

  • Governor may address and send message to Legislative Assembly or Council or both houses assembled together.

Article 176: Special Address by the Governor

  • (1) At the commencement of first session of after general elections and the first session of each year, Governor addresses Legislature.

Article 177: Rights of Ministers and Advocate General

  • Ministers and Advocate General can participate in debates and proceedings but cannot vote if they are not a member of the House.

Article 178: Speaker and Deputy Speaker of Legislative Assembly

  • Legislative Assembly elects a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker.

Article 179: Vacation and Resignation or Removal of Speaker/Deputy Speaker

  • to be done by resolution passed by majority of the Assembly members.

Article 180: Duties of Deputy Speaker

  • Deputy Speaker acts as the Speaker when office is vacant or Speaker is absent.

Article 181: Speaker/Deputy Speaker not to preside during consideration of resolution for their own removal

Article 182: Chairman and Deputy Chairman of Legislative Council.

Article 183: Vacation, Resignation, Removal of Chairman/Deputy Chairman

  • Similar to provisions for Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

Article 184: Duties of Deputy Chairman

  • Deputy Chairman acts as Chairman when office is vacant or chairman is absent.

Article 185: Chairman or Deputy Chairman shall not preside when his removal resolution is being considered.

Article 186: Salaries and Allowances of Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman, Deputy Chairman

  • Salaries and allowances are determined by State Legislature.

Article 187: Secretariat of State Legislature

  • Appointed and regulated by State Legislature.

Article 188: Oath or Affirmation by Members

Article 189: Voting in Houses, Vacancies, and Quorum

  • (1) All questions in Legislature decided by majority of members present and voting.
  • (2) Presiding officer can vote in the first instance and also have a casting vote.
  • (3) Legislature can act despite vacancies.
  • (4) Quorum for a meeting = 10% of total membership.

Article 190: Vacation of Seats

Seat vacated if:

  • a person is member of both the houses,
  • member resigns,
  • a member becomes subject to disqualification

Article 191: Disqualifications of Membership

Disqualification if:

  • Holds office of profit.
  • Unsound mind.
  • Undischarged insolvent.
  • Disqualified under anti-defection laws or other Parliament-made laws.

Article 192: Decision on Disqualification

Article 193: Penalty for Sitting and Voting before taking Oath or when disqualified: fine decided by Legislature.

Article 194: Powers, Privileges, and Immunities of State Legislatures and Their Members

Article 195: Salaries and Allowances of Members

Article 196: Introduction and Passing of Bills

  • Bills can originate in either House (if bicameral).
  • Bill must be passed by both Houses and assented by Governor to become a law.
  • In case of an Ordinary bill, Legislative Assembly has upper hand over Legislative Council.
  • When a bill originates in the LC, and if LA disagrees, then the bill lapses, and there is no provision for joint sitting in Part VI.

What happens when a bill originates in LA - two cases:

  1. 1. LA → LC → Governor
  2. 2. LA → LC → Governor (Bill returned to LA)
  • In 2nd case, LC can only delay an Ordinary Bill by maximum 4 months i.e. 3 months in first instance and for 1 month in 2nd instance.

Article 197: Restriction on Powers of Legislative Council as to bills other than Money bill

Article 198: Special Procedure for Money Bills

  • Money Bill can be introduced only in Legislative Assembly.
  • then sent to Legislative Council for recommendations. LC cannot reject the bill, it must return the bill within 14 days, with or without recommendations, if the council fails to do so, the money bill is deemed passed in its original form.

Article 199: Definition of Money Bill

Article 200: Assent to Bills by the Governor

Article 201: Bills Reserved for President's Consideration

Article 202: Annual Financial Statement (Budget)

Article 203: Procedure in Legislature with Respect to Estimates

  • Demands for grants made only on the recommendation of the Governor.

Article 204: Appropriation Bills

Article 205: Supplementary, Additional, and Excess Grants

Article 206: Votes on Account, Votes of Credit, and Exceptional Grants.

Article 207: Special Provisions for Financial Bills

  • Money Bills require prior recommendation of the Governor for introduction.
